content:
mike: Observed increased WS handshake latency for eu-west clients this morning, causing ~3% more reconnects. Console shows a cluster of slow handshakes from a handful of edge nodes.

sara: Ugh. Any correlation to deploys or config changes?

mike: No deploys. Looks like a routing wobble: connections for eu-west are getting routed through a central proxy in us-east for some customers. TLDR: added ~4s of RTT.

jamal: Do we have metrics that tag handshake duration with routed_via/edge_node?

linda: Our console sampling currently only surfaces handshake_ms percentile per region, not per proxy hop. We sampled 1% at the time; might have missed early signals.

ops-bot: New alert: ws_handshake_95p > 2s in eu-west — triggered by mike at 4387654321

sara: Can you paste an example log?

mike: Sure. snippet: `[conn id=abc123] region=eu-west client_ip=2.2.2.2 routed_via=us-east-proxy-9 ws_handshake_ms=4123 tls_ms=200 tcp_rtt_ms=180`

jamal: That routed_via jump is suspicious. We changed routing fallback last month to prefer capacity availability over geo for low-tier tenants — maybe hitting that policy.

linda: Console: sampling shows handshake p95 eu-west=1.8s but when I filter for routed_via!=local, p95 spikes to 4.3s. Sampling rate might be biasing observed percentiles down.

mike: Two parts to fix: 1) temporarily adjust routing policy so eu-west pref geo for a canary cohort; 2) increase handshake telemetry sample for next 2 hours so console dashboards show hop-level breakdown.

jamal: Agreed. Also can we short-circuit WS handshake timers at proxies so they don't amplify RTT? E.g., reduce proxy-side idle/hard timeouts that trigger reconnects.

sara: Reducing timeouts risks churn elsewhere. I'd rather fix routing policy first and monitor.

linda: I'll flip sampling to 25% for ws_handshake_hop tag and add dashboard panel for routed_via breakdown. Will also annotate the existing p95 chart so ops can see the cohort.

mike: I'll prepare a config change: rollback the low-tier fallback to prefer local for eu regions (canary 5% of traffic). Will post PR link.

jamal: I'll add a short-lived alert: ws_handshake_p95_by_hop > 3s for more than 2mins. Also will run a probe from eu edge to confirm end-to-end path.

ops-bot: mike requested deploy of routing-config-canary -> queued (PR: #4567)

mike: PR link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/configs/pulls/4567 — canary targets low-tier customer set in eu-west.

linda: Dashboard updated, sampling at 25% now — adding annotation for canary start.

jamal: Probe result: confirmed path via us-east-proxy-9, handshake ~4.1s. A couple of proxys report elevated cpu (75-85%) during the window.

sara: Could be transient overload causing us-east proxies to accept some eu connections due to capacity heuristic. For prod fix we should: (A) tweak capacity scoring to favor geo when latency delta > 300ms, (B) add health signals to not accept cross-region routings when cpu>70%. Thoughts?

mike: +1 to both. For now, canary rollback looks safe. Post-canary we should update scoring logic and add the proxy cpu gating.

linda: Will create a console alert to surface cross-region routed sessions and CPU on those proxies in one view. That should help SRE detect recurrence faster.

jamal: Action items: 1) mike deploy canary (in progress), 2) linda increase sampling and create cross-region dashboard (done/in progress), 3) jamal add short-lived hop alert and run probes (done), 4) sara to spec scoring change and cpu gating RFC.

mike: Canary just rolled out to 5% at 4387654335. Early metrics: p95 eu-west handshake down from 1.8s->1.5s overall, and for routed_via!=local down from 4.3s->2.2s.

linda: Console shows fewer cross-region sessions. Annotation added. :thumbsup:

sara: I'll draft RFC for scoring + cpu gating today and tag eng-platform/eng-sre.

jamal: Leaving the short-lived alert on for 30m, then we'll reassess. If no regression, plan to roll the routing change to 50% tomorrow.

mike: Thanks everyone. Follow-up: we should consider surfaces in the Console rollout UX to make it easier to compare per-hop and per-region percentiles — saved search maybe. Logged feature request: https://git.internal/r/redwood/console/issues/912

linda: Nice. That saved-search idea will help reduce blind spots caused by low sampling.

ops-bot: Routing canary 5% -> success at 4387654337
